label: prop:pn-averaging-uniqueness
title: Canonical p-n interface averaging uniqueness
html:
Let \sigma_{pn} and \sigma_{pn}' be two p-n interface averaging functionals on H_{3A}(R, q). Assume both satisfy: (a) bar-invariance

  \sigma_{pn}(q) = \sigma_{pn}(q^{-1}),

(b) color-flavor compatibility, and (c) standard normalisation \sigma_{pn} = z. Then they are equal block-wise. The canonical p-n averaging is uniquely determined.

Setting

The QOU mass identity at A \geq 2 contracts a per-interface averaging functional \sigma_{pn} across the p-n boundary slice. The two production candidates are the uniform bar-invariant form z - h/2 and the Bring color-tube weighted form z - h(1/2 - \delta/4). Once we fix color-flavor compatibility, the averaging is uniquely determined within the class satisfying (a)–(c).

Scope of (a) — corrected. An earlier version of this paragraph stated that both candidates satisfy bar-invariance. Only the uniform form does. Writing \overline{\phantom{x}} for q \mapsto q^{-1}, the flavour split is bar-mixed, \overline{\delta} = -q^{2}\delta, and

  \overline{\sigma_{pn}^{\,\mathrm{weighted}}} - \sigma_{pn}^{\,\mathrm{weighted}}
  \;=\; \frac{(q-1)^{5}(q+1)^{3}(q^{2}+1)}{12\,q^{5}}
  \;\neq\; 0
  \quad (q \neq 1),

about 1.67 \times 10^{-5} at the substrate anchor, whereas the uniform form satisfies (a) exactly — it is the bar-symmetriser \tfrac12(z + \overline{z}) of the p-p factor, since \overline{z} = z - h (prf:interface-knot-markov-z). Verified exactly in pn_interface_bar_structure_probe.py.

The Lean is unaffected: pn_averaging_unique carries BarInvariant as an instance hypothesis and proves only the implication, so it is silent on which candidate discharges it. What was wrong was restating the antecedent as established for both — a conditional hypothesis reported as a settled fact.

The consequence is one of scope, and is recorded rather than resolved: the uniqueness statement covers the bar-invariant class, and the colour-weighted convention lies outside its hypotheses. This does not say the colour weighting is wrong, and it does not by itself bear on which convention should be canonical.

Derivation chain for the closed-form weight

The substrate evaluation w(t, t', q) = 1/(1 - h_q \cdot q^{10}) derives from Bring's surface geometry:

  • Bring's surface has genus g = 4.
  • The genus-4 force-carrier pair is \{T(2,9), T(3,5)\}.
  • We prove \alpha_{\text{shift}}(T_{p,k}) = k \cdot (p-1). For T(3,5), \alpha_{\text{shift}}(T(3,5)) = 10. This specifies the pole order of \sigma.
  • The Bring color-tube weight inherits this derived pole order q^{10}.

Lean structure

We stage the uniqueness via the conditional-class pattern:

  • BarInvariant R σ_pn: the bar-involution axiom.
  • ColorFlavorCompatible R σ_pn: the open class for color-sheet mapping.
  • StandardNorm R σ_pn z: the pointwise normalisation.

Conditional on these classes, theorem pn_averaging_unique proves \sigma_{pn} = \sigma_{pn}'.
